```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")
```

**This analysis is exploratory.** It was specified on 9 October 2026, after
the registered results of all five studies were known, and no registration
names it. Nothing in this report tests a registered hypothesis. Every table
it writes, and the pairs file it reads, says so in its first column,
`analysis`, and the figure says so in its caption.

# 0. What this file does

In Studies 2, 4 and 5 each participant explained the same source artwork at
three levels of modification, None, Slight and Dramatic, once for each rating
question. `ExplanationShift_01_Measure.ipynb` measured, without seeing the
label or the rating, how far each participant's explanation of one source
moved between two levels. It measured the move in two ways.

- The embedding distance. A sentence-embedding model is a network trained
  beforehand on other text that turns a sentence into a list of numbers, so
  that sentences with similar meanings get similar lists. The locally stored
  model all-mpnet-base-v2 turns each explanation into 768 numbers. The
  cosine similarity of two lists is 1 when they point the same way and 0
  when they are unrelated, and the embedding distance is 1 minus it.
- The word distance. A content word is a word left once a fixed list of
  function words, such as *the* and *of*, is removed. The Jaccard overlap of
  two explanations is the number of content words both use divided by the
  number either uses, and the word distance is 1 minus it.

Beside each distance the notebook put a stranger baseline, the mean distance
from the participant's first-level explanation to other participants'
second-level explanations of the same image and question. This file joins the
source label, Human or AI, back on and asks two questions.

1. **Do the explanations of AI-arm participants move less?** The shift of one
   participant on one source image and question is the None to Dramatic
   distance minus its stranger baseline. A shift of zero means the
   participant's Dramatic explanation lies as far from their own None
   explanation as other participants' Dramatic explanations do. A negative
   shift means it stayed closer to their own None explanation. If an AI
   source taints the second work, that is, if its origin counts against the
   work however much Alex changed it, AI-arm participants keep writing about
   where the source came from at every level, their explanations move less,
   and AI minus Human in the shift is negative. If raters judge what Alex
   added, the two arms move about as far and the difference is near zero.
   Creativity is the primary question; transformativeness and essence change
   are secondary.
2. **Does talk of origin persist as the work changes?** From each study's
   deposited text measures: the share of explanations that mention prompting
   or a machine, and the share that state a machine made the work, at each
   level and in each arm. Under taint, origin talk in the AI arm should stay
   up at Dramatic. If raters turn to what Alex added, it should fall as the
   work changes.

Every explanation was written after its rating, so nothing here says what
produced a rating. It describes what people wrote once their number was
chosen.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. lme4 and
# lmerTest fit the mixed models, and emmeans gives the contrasts with their
# intervals. ggplot2 and patchwork draw the figure.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})
```

## 1.2 Paths and constants

```{r paths}
# Every path is found from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory when the file is knitted. EXPLANATION_SHIFT_DIR names this folder
# instead, and STUDY_SHARED_R the folder of the shared R helpers. Printed
# paths are relative to the pipeline folder, two levels up.
HERE <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("EXPLANATION_SHIFT_DIR", getwd()), mustWork = TRUE)
PIPELINE_DIR <- normalizePath(file.path(HERE, "..", ".."), mustWork = TRUE)
SHARED_R <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_R", file.path(PIPELINE_DIR, "shared", "R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "text_checks.R"))
show <- function(p) relative_path(p, PIPELINE_DIR)

TABLES  <- file.path(HERE, "tables")
FIGURES <- file.path(HERE, "figures")
dir.create(TABLES, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(FIGURES, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Each study's files. Studies 2 and 5 store the Human or AI label in the
# column source, and Study 4 in the column label. The measures files name the
# source image stimulus_image in Studies 2 and 5 and stimulus_source in
# Study 4.
STUDY_LEVELS <- c("Study 2", "Study 4", "Study 5")
STUDY_FILES <- tibble(study = STUDY_LEVELS,
                      label_column = c("source", "label", "source"),
                      measures_image = c("stimulus_image", "stimulus_source", "stimulus_image")) %>%
  mutate(n = sub("Study ", "", study),
         folder = file.path(PIPELINE_DIR, study),
         long = file.path(folder, paste0("study", n, "_long_with_text.csv")),
         measures = file.path(folder, "nlp", paste0("study", n, "_text_measures.csv")),
         quant_manifest = file.path(folder, "tables", paste0("study", n, "_quant_run_manifest.csv")),
         text_manifest = file.path(folder, "tables", paste0("study", n, "_text_run_manifest.csv")))

INPUTS <- c(pairs = file.path(HERE, "nlp", "explanation_shift_pairs.csv"),
            setNames(STUDY_FILES$long, paste0("study", STUDY_FILES$n, "_long")),
            setNames(STUDY_FILES$measures, paste0("study", STUDY_FILES$n, "_measures")))
MEASURE_MANIFEST <- file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_measure_run_manifest.csv")
missing_inputs <- names(INPUTS)[!file.exists(INPUTS)]
if (length(missing_inputs) > 0) {
  stop("Missing input(s): ", paste(missing_inputs, collapse = ", "),
       ". Run ExplanationShift_01_Measure.ipynb first.")
}

# The constants of the analysis. The R seed is the one the registrations
# name for R, and the numbers of permutations and resamples are those of the
# registered text checks.
SEED         <- 20260421L
N_PERM       <- 200L
N_BOOT       <- 2000L
LABEL_LEVELS <- c("Human", "AI")
LEVELS       <- c("None", "Slight", "Dramatic")
DIMENSIONS   <- c("creativity", "transformativeness", "essence_change")
ROLE         <- c(creativity = "primary", transformativeness = "secondary",
                  essence_change = "secondary")
DISTANCES    <- c(embedding = "emb", word = "word")
CONTROL      <- lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
EXPLORATORY  <- paste("exploratory: specified on 9 October 2026, after the registered",
                      "results of all five studies were known; no registration names it")

# Every table carries the analysis status in its first column.
write_table <- function(df, name) {
  write_csv(df %>% mutate(analysis = EXPLORATORY, .before = 1),
            file.path(TABLES, name), na = "")
}
for (p in names(INPUTS)) cat(sprintf("%-15s %s\n", p, show(INPUTS[[p]])))
cat("Tables to:      ", show(TABLES), "\nFigures to:     ", show(FIGURES), "\n")
```

## 1.3 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record stores the SHA-256 checksum of every input (a 64-character
# fingerprint of the file's exact bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest
# now and each output's previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and
# writes the manifest last.
run <- start_run_record(INPUTS, file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_analysis_run_manifest.csv"),
                        HERE)
run$inputs <- run$inputs %>% mutate(file = show(INPUTS), analysis = EXPLORATORY, .before = 1)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_analysis_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")

# Each input must be the file its producing run recorded: the pairs file in
# the measurement notebook's manifest, each long data file in its study's
# quantitative manifest, and each measures file in its study's text manifest.
# The long data files must also be the ones the notebook read.
if (!file.exists(MEASURE_MANIFEST)) {
  stop("The measurement notebook's manifest is missing. Run ",
       "ExplanationShift_01_Measure.ipynb to its end first.")
}
measure_manifest <- read_csv(MEASURE_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE)
producer <- bind_rows(
  measure_manifest %>% filter(role == "output") %>%
    transmute(file, recorded_sha256 = sha256, producer = basename(MEASURE_MANIFEST)),
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(STUDY_FILES)), function(k) {
    s <- STUDY_FILES[k, ]
    bind_rows(
      read_csv(s$quant_manifest, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
        transmute(file = file.path(s$study, file), recorded_sha256 = sha256,
                  producer = basename(s$quant_manifest)),
      read_csv(s$text_manifest, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% distinct(file, sha256) %>%
        transmute(file = file.path(s$study, file), recorded_sha256 = sha256,
                  producer = basename(s$text_manifest)))
  })))
read_by_notebook <- measure_manifest %>% filter(role == "input") %>%
  transmute(file, read_by_notebook_sha256 = sha256)
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_input_check.csv"))
input_check <- tibble(input = names(INPUTS), file = show(INPUTS),
                      sha256 = run$inputs$sha256) %>%
  left_join(producer, by = "file") %>%
  left_join(read_by_notebook, by = "file") %>%
  mutate(matches_producer = sha256 == recorded_sha256,
         matches_notebook_input = if_else(grepl("_long$", input),
                                          sha256 == read_by_notebook_sha256, NA))
write_table(input_check, "explanation_shift_input_check.csv")
print(as.data.frame(select(input_check, input, file, producer, matches_producer,
                           matches_notebook_input)))
stopifnot(all(input_check$matches_producer %in% TRUE),
          all(input_check$matches_notebook_input[grepl("_long$", input_check$input)] %in% TRUE))
```

# 2. The data

## 2.1 The pairs and the labels

```{r pairs-and-labels}
# The pairs file holds one row per participant, source image, question and
# pair of levels, with no label and no rating. Its first column states the
# analysis status; the check below reads it and then drops it.
PAIR_COLUMNS <- c("analysis", "study", "id", "image", "dimension", "pair", "emb_distance",
                  "emb_stranger", "word_distance", "word_stranger", "words_a", "words_b")
pairs <- read_csv(INPUTS[["pairs"]], na = "", progress = FALSE,
                  col_types = cols(analysis = col_character(),
                                   study = col_character(), id = col_character(),
                                   image = col_character(), dimension = col_character(),
                                   pair = col_character(), emb_distance = col_double(),
                                   emb_stranger = col_double(), word_distance = col_double(),
                                   word_stranger = col_double(), words_a = col_integer(),
                                   words_b = col_integer()))
stopifnot(identical(names(pairs), PAIR_COLUMNS), all(pairs$analysis == EXPLORATORY),
          all(pairs$study %in% STUDY_LEVELS), all(pairs$dimension %in% DIMENSIONS),
          all(pairs$pair %in% c("None-Slight", "Slight-Dramatic", "None-Dramatic")))
pairs <- select(pairs, -analysis)

# The label of each participant, read from the study's long data file, whose
# label_mode must say "real" on every row.
labels <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(STUDY_FILES)), function(k) {
  s <- STUDY_FILES[k, ]
  d <- read_csv(s$long, col_select = all_of(c("id", s$label_column, "label_mode")),
                col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), progress = FALSE)
  if (!all(d$label_mode == "real")) stop(s$study, "'s long data file is not from a real-label run.")
  d %>% distinct(id, source = .data[[s$label_column]]) %>% mutate(study = s$study, .before = 1)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(labels[c("study", "id")]), all(labels$source %in% LABEL_LEVELS))
print(as.data.frame(count(labels, study, source) %>%
                      pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = n)))

pairs <- pairs %>% left_join(labels, by = c("study", "id"), relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  mutate(source = factor(source, levels = LABEL_LEVELS))
stopifnot(!anyNA(pairs$source),
          identical(sort(unique(paste(pairs$study, pairs$id))),
                    sort(unique(paste(labels$study, labels$id)))))
cat("Pairs:", nrow(pairs), "| complete sets of three:", nrow(pairs) / 3,
    "| participants:", n_distinct(paste(pairs$study, pairs$id)), "\n")
```

## 2.2 What the distances look like

```{r description}
# Means over every pair of levels, by study, arm and question, as
# description. A shift is a distance minus its stranger baseline. Word
# distances are missing where an explanation has no content word, and their
# means are over the rest.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_description.csv"))
description <- pairs %>%
  mutate(pair = factor(pair, levels = c("None-Slight", "Slight-Dramatic", "None-Dramatic")),
         dimension = factor(dimension, levels = DIMENSIONS),
         emb_shift = emb_distance - emb_stranger,
         word_shift = word_distance - word_stranger) %>%
  group_by(study, source, dimension, pair) %>%
  summarise(n_participants = n_distinct(id), n_sets = n(),
            emb_distance = mean(emb_distance), emb_stranger = mean(emb_stranger),
            emb_shift = mean(emb_shift),
            n_sets_word = sum(!is.na(word_shift)),
            word_distance = mean(word_distance, na.rm = TRUE),
            word_stranger = mean(word_stranger[!is.na(word_shift)]),
            word_shift = mean(word_shift, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_words = mean((words_a + words_b) / 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(dimension, study, pair, source)
write_table(description, "explanation_shift_description.csv")
print(as.data.frame(description %>% filter(dimension == "creativity") %>%
                      select(study, source, pair, n_sets, emb_distance, emb_stranger,
                             emb_shift, word_distance, word_stranger, word_shift) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))))
```

# 3. Do the explanations of AI-arm participants move less?

## 3.1 The model

The shift of one participant on one source image and question is the None to
Dramatic distance minus its stranger baseline, computed separately for the
embedding distance and the word distance. For each question and each kind of
distance, a linear mixed model (a regression with an estimated adjustment for
each participant and each source image) is fitted:

    shift ~ source * study + words_c + (1 | study:id) + (1 | image)

Here `source` is the label (Human or AI), `study` is Study 2, 4 or 5, and
`(1 | study:id)` and `(1 | image)` give each participant and each source image
its own adjustment to the mean. `words_c` is the mean number of distinct
content words in the two explanations, centred on its mean in the model's
data (that mean subtracted), because how far two texts lie apart depends on
how much each says. The model is fitted by restricted maximum likelihood (REML,
the usual estimator of the variances in a mixed model) with the bobyqa
optimizer (the routine that searches for the best-fitting values), as in the
study files.

From each fit, estimated marginal means (the model's predicted mean shift for
each arm, at the average length) give AI minus Human within each study and
pooled over the three studies with equal weight. Each has a 95 percent
interval with Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom (an approximation that sets
the reference t distribution from the model's variances). A word distance is
missing where an explanation has no content word, so the word models use the
rest.

## 3.2 The permutation null

The model's interval rests on the model's assumptions. The permutation null
asks the same question without them. The labels are dealt out afresh among
the participants within each study, so every study keeps its number in each
arm and every participant keeps one label, the model is refitted, and the
four AI minus Human differences are recorded; this is done 200 times. The
p-value is the share of shuffles, counting the observed data as one, whose
difference lies at least as far from zero as the observed one. The 200
shuffles are drawn from seed 20260421 before the parallel section starts, the
same shuffles serve all six models, and the refits run on up to eight
processor cores.

```{r shift-models}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_models.csv"),
                  file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_arm_means.csv"))

# One row per participant, source image and question: the None to Dramatic
# shift on each kind of distance, and the mean length of the two explanations.
shift <- pairs %>% filter(pair == "None-Dramatic") %>%
  mutate(shift_emb = emb_distance - emb_stranger,
         shift_word = word_distance - word_stranger,
         mean_words = (words_a + words_b) / 2,
         key = paste(study, id, sep = "|"))

FORMULA <- y ~ source * study + words_c + (1 | study:id) + (1 | image)

model_data <- function(dim, distance) {
  shift %>% filter(dimension == dim) %>%
    mutate(y = .data[[paste0("shift_", DISTANCES[[distance]])]]) %>%
    filter(!is.na(y)) %>%
    mutate(words_c = mean_words - mean(mean_words),
           source = factor(source, levels = LABEL_LEVELS),
           study = factor(study, levels = STUDY_LEVELS),
           id = factor(id), image = factor(image))
}

fit_log <- list()
fit_logged <- function(expr, step, d) {
  res <- fit_with_status(expr)
  fit_log[[step]] <<- bind_cols(tibble(step = step, n_obs = nrow(d)), res$status)
  res
}

# The 200 shuffles: within each study, the labels are dealt out again among
# its participants, taken in byte order of their identifiers.
participants <- labels %>% mutate(key = paste(study, id, sep = "|")) %>%
  filter(key %in% shift$key)
participants <- participants[order(participants$study, participants$id, method = "radix"), ]
set.seed(SEED)
shuffles <- replicate(N_PERM, {
  lab <- participants$source
  for (s in STUDY_LEVELS) {
    ix <- which(participants$study == s)
    lab[ix] <- lab[ix][sample.int(length(ix))]
  }
  setNames(lab, participants$key)
}, simplify = FALSE)
arm_sizes <- table(participants$study, participants$source)
stopifnot(all(vapply(shuffles, function(lab) {
  all(table(participants$study, lab) == arm_sizes)
}, logical(1))))

# The AI minus Human differences from one refit on shuffled labels, and
# whether that refit converged. A refit that fails gives NA and is counted.
perm_once <- function(lab, d, L) {
  d$source <- factor(lab[d$key], levels = LABEL_LEVELS)
  res <- suppressMessages(fit_with_status(
    lme4::lmer(FORMULA, data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL)))
  if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(L) + 1))
  c(as.numeric(L %*% lme4::fixef(res$fit)), as.numeric(isTRUE(res$status$converged)))
}

SCOPES <- c("pooled over studies, equal weight", STUDY_LEVELS)
shift_model <- function(dim, distance) {
  d <- model_data(dim, distance)
  step <- paste0("3 shift, ", dim, ", ", distance, " distance")
  res <- fit_logged(lmerTest::lmer(FORMULA, data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL), step, d)
  usable <- fit_usable(res$status)
  counts <- d %>% distinct(study, id, source) %>% count(study, source) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = n)
  n_by_scope <- bind_rows(
    tibble(scope = SCOPES[1], n_obs = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$key),
           n_human = sum(counts$Human), n_ai = sum(counts$AI)),
    tibble(scope = STUDY_LEVELS,
           n_obs = as.integer(table(factor(d$study, STUDY_LEVELS))),
           n_participants = as.integer(tapply(d$key, factor(d$study, STUDY_LEVELS), n_distinct)),
           n_human = counts$Human[match(STUDY_LEVELS, counts$study)],
           n_ai = counts$AI[match(STUDY_LEVELS, counts$study)]))
  if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) {
    return(list(contrasts = n_by_scope %>% mutate(dimension = dim, distance = distance,
                                                  note = fit_note(res$status)),
                means = NULL))
  }

  # The estimated marginal means of each arm, within each study and pooled
  # over the studies with equal weight, and AI minus Human in each.
  emm_study <- emmeans::emmeans(res$fit, ~ source | study, lmer.df = "satterthwaite",
                                lmerTest.limit = 1e5)
  emm_pool  <- suppressMessages(emmeans::emmeans(res$fit, ~ source, lmer.df = "satterthwaite",
                                                 lmerTest.limit = 1e5))
  con_study <- emmeans::contrast(emm_study, list("AI minus Human" = c(-1, 1)))
  con_pool  <- emmeans::contrast(emm_pool, list("AI minus Human" = c(-1, 1)))
  con <- bind_rows(as_tibble(summary(con_pool, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))) %>%
                     mutate(scope = SCOPES[1]),
                   as_tibble(summary(con_study, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))) %>%
                     mutate(scope = as.character(study)))
  stopifnot(identical(con$scope, SCOPES))

  # The same four differences as linear combinations of the fixed effects,
  # so that each refit gives them without recomputing the marginal means.
  L <- rbind(con_pool@linfct, con_study@linfct)
  stopifnot(ncol(L) == length(lme4::fixef(res$fit)),
            isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(L %*% lme4::fixef(res$fit)), con$estimate,
                             tolerance = 1e-8)))
  null <- matrix(text_run_permutations(shuffles, function(lab) perm_once(lab, d, L),
                                       text_default_workers()),
                 nrow = N_PERM, byrow = TRUE)
  null_est <- null[, seq_len(nrow(L)), drop = FALSE]
  n_valid <- colSums(!is.na(null_est))
  p_perm <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(L)), function(j) {
    (1 + sum(abs(null_est[, j]) >= abs(con$estimate[j]), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + n_valid[j])
  }, numeric(1))

  contrasts <- con %>%
    transmute(scope, quantity = "AI minus Human in the None to Dramatic shift",
              estimate, se = SE, df,
              ci_lo = na_unless_usable(lower.CL, res$status),
              ci_hi = na_unless_usable(upper.CL, res$status),
              t = t.ratio, p_model = na_unless_usable(p.value, res$status)) %>%
    mutate(p_perm = na_unless_usable(p_perm, res$status),
           null_lo = apply(null_est, 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
           null_hi = apply(null_est, 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
           n_perm = N_PERM, n_perm_valid = n_valid,
           n_perm_converged = sum(null[, ncol(null)] == 1, na.rm = TRUE), perm_seed = SEED) %>%
    left_join(n_by_scope, by = "scope") %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim, role = ROLE[[dim]], distance = distance,
           converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
           note = fit_note(res$status))

  means <- bind_rows(as_tibble(summary(emm_pool, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE))) %>%
                       mutate(scope = SCOPES[1]),
                     as_tibble(summary(emm_study, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE))) %>%
                       mutate(scope = as.character(study))) %>%
    transmute(dimension = dim, role = ROLE[[dim]], distance = distance, scope,
              arm = as.character(source), mean_shift = emmean, se = SE, df,
              ci_lo = na_unless_usable(lower.CL, res$status),
              ci_hi = na_unless_usable(upper.CL, res$status),
              note = "estimated marginal mean at the average length")
  list(contrasts = contrasts, means = means)
}

started <- Sys.time()
fits <- list()
for (dim in DIMENSIONS) for (distance in names(DISTANCES)) {
  fits[[paste(dim, distance)]] <- shift_model(dim, distance)
  cat(sprintf("%-18s %-9s fitted, 200 permutations done, %.1f minutes so far\n", dim, distance,
              as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins"))))
}

models <- bind_rows(lapply(fits, `[[`, "contrasts")) %>%
  mutate(reading = case_when(
    is.na(ci_lo) | is.na(ci_hi) ~ NA_character_,
    ci_hi < 0 ~ "AI explanations moved less, as taint predicts",
    ci_lo > 0 ~ "AI explanations moved more, against the taint prediction",
    TRUE ~ "no difference shown: the 95 percent interval includes zero"),
    predicted_under_taint = "negative") %>%
  relocate(dimension, role, distance, scope, quantity, estimate, se, df, ci_lo, ci_hi,
           p_model, p_perm, reading)
arm_means <- bind_rows(lapply(fits, `[[`, "means"))
write_table(models, "explanation_shift_models.csv")
write_table(arm_means, "explanation_shift_arm_means.csv")
```

## 3.3 What the models say

The table holds 24 rows: three questions, two kinds of distance, and the
pooled and three within-study differences of each. No interval is widened
and no p-value raised to allow for the number of rows, so even if the label changed
nothing, about one row in twenty would have a 95 percent interval clear of
zero by chance alone.

```{r shift-results}
print(as.data.frame(models %>%
  select(dimension, distance, scope, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi, p_model, p_perm, n_perm_valid) %>%
  mutate(across(c(estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi), ~ round(.x, 4)),
         across(c(p_model, p_perm), ~ round(.x, 3)))))

# The pooled result of each model in words, with the arm means beside it.
for (k in which(models$scope == SCOPES[1])) {
  r <- models[k, ]
  am <- arm_means %>% filter(dimension == r$dimension, distance == r$distance, scope == SCOPES[1])
  cat(sprintf(paste0("%s (%s), %s distance: mean shift Human %.4f, AI %.4f; AI minus Human %.4f, ",
                     "95%% interval %.4f to %.4f, permutation p = %.3f. %s.\n"),
              r$dimension, r$role, r$distance,
              am$mean_shift[am$arm == "Human"], am$mean_shift[am$arm == "AI"],
              r$estimate, r$ci_lo, r$ci_hi, r$p_perm,
              if (is.na(r$reading)) "No reading: the fit is not usable" else
                paste0(toupper(substring(r$reading, 1, 1)), substring(r$reading, 2))))
}
```

# 4. Does talk of origin persist as the work changes?

Each study's text notebook applied Study 1's word lists to every explanation
without seeing the label or the rating. Two of its columns are used here.
`says_prompt` is true when an explanation mentions prompting, typing or
generating, or names a machine or an image generator. The machine-made
reading is "asserted" when an explanation states, plainly or as an impression,
that a machine made the work, and it sets aside phrases that are denied or sit
in a supposition.

The measures are joined to the label through each study's own keys, the
participant, the second work and the question, one row to one row. The shares
are then taken over the same explanations as section 3: the complete sets of
three, so the share at None and the share at Dramatic come from the same
people writing about the same images. Each share is the number of explanations
that carry the mark divided by the number of explanations, in each study, arm
and level, over the three questions together and for each question.

The intervals come from 2,000 resamples of participants within each study
and arm, drawn from seed 20260421. A resample draws as many participants as
the arm holds, with replacement, so one participant can be drawn more than
once and another not at all, and each arm keeps its size. Each interval is
the middle 95 percent of the resampled values.
Pooled values are the mean of the three studies, each study weighted equally,
computed within each resample. Beside the shares sit the change from None to
Dramatic in each arm, AI minus Human at each level, and AI minus Human in the
change. Under taint, the AI arm's change is near zero; if origin talk falls as
the work changes, it is negative.

```{r origin-talk}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_origin_talk.csv"))

# The measures, joined to each study's keys and labels. The measures files
# carry no label and no rating; the join adds the label only.
origin <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(STUDY_FILES)), function(k) {
  s <- STUDY_FILES[k, ]
  m <- read_csv(s$measures, na = character(), progress = FALSE,
                col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
  need <- c("id", "stimulus_id", s$measures_image, "stimulus_modification", "dimension",
            "says_prompt", "machine_made_reading")
  stopifnot(all(need %in% names(m)),
            !any(c("rating", "label", "Type", "source_time", "editing_time",
                   "condition", "response_text") %in% names(m)))
  keys <- read_csv(s$long, col_select = all_of(c("id", "work_id", "dimension")),
                   col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), progress = FALSE)
  joined <- m %>% select(all_of(need)) %>%
    inner_join(keys, by = c("id", "stimulus_id" = "work_id", "dimension"),
               relationship = "one-to-one")
  stopifnot(nrow(joined) == nrow(m), nrow(joined) == nrow(keys))
  joined %>% transmute(study = s$study, id, image = .data[[s$measures_image]],
                       level = stimulus_modification, dimension, says_prompt,
                       machine_made_reading)
})) %>%
  left_join(labels, by = c("study", "id"), relationship = "many-to-one")
stopifnot(!anyNA(origin$source), all(origin$says_prompt %in% c("True", "False")),
          all(origin$machine_made_reading %in% c("asserted", "not_asserted", "neither")),
          all(origin$level %in% LEVELS))
origin <- origin %>% mutate(prompt = says_prompt == "True",
                            machine = machine_made_reading == "asserted")

# The same explanations as section 3: the complete sets of three.
sets <- pairs %>% distinct(study, id, image, dimension)
origin <- origin %>% semi_join(sets, by = c("study", "id", "image", "dimension"))
stopifnot(nrow(origin) == 3 * nrow(sets),
          all(count(origin, study, id, image, dimension)$n == 3))
cat("Explanations in the complete sets:", nrow(origin), "\n")

# Per participant, level and question: the number of explanations and how
# many carry each mark. The rows for all three questions sum the questions.
QUESTIONS <- c("all three questions", DIMENSIONS)
per_person <- bind_rows(
  origin %>% group_by(study, id, source, level) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), prompt = sum(prompt), machine = sum(machine), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(question = QUESTIONS[1]),
  origin %>% group_by(study, id, source, level, question = dimension) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), prompt = sum(prompt), machine = sum(machine), .groups = "drop"))
CELLS <- as.vector(outer(QUESTIONS, LEVELS, paste, sep = "|"))
MEASURE_NAMES <- c(prompt = "mentions prompting or a machine (says_prompt)",
                   machine = "states that a machine made the work (machine-made reading asserted)")

# Each study's counts as matrices, one row per participant and one column per
# question and level.
study_matrices <- lapply(STUDY_LEVELS, function(s) {
  pp <- per_person %>% filter(study == s)
  ids <- sort(unique(pp$id), method = "radix")
  arm <- labels$source[labels$study == s][match(ids, labels$id[labels$study == s])]
  fill <- function(col) {
    m <- matrix(0, length(ids), length(CELLS), dimnames = list(ids, CELLS))
    m[cbind(match(pp$id, ids), match(paste(pp$question, pp$level, sep = "|"), CELLS))] <- pp[[col]]
    m
  }
  list(ids = ids, arm = arm, n = fill("n"), prompt = fill("prompt"), machine = fill("machine"))
})
names(study_matrices) <- STUDY_LEVELS

# Every quantity of the section from the shares of one study, or of one
# resample: shares by arm and level, the change from None to Dramatic in
# each arm, AI minus Human at each level, and AI minus Human in the change.
quantities <- function(share) {
  out <- list()
  for (m in names(MEASURE_NAMES)) for (q in QUESTIONS) {
    at <- function(arm, level) share[[arm]][[m]][, paste(q, level, sep = "|")]
    for (a in LABEL_LEVELS) {
      for (l in LEVELS) out[[paste(m, q, a, l, sep = "|")]] <- at(a, l)
      out[[paste(m, q, a, "Dramatic minus None", sep = "|")]] <- at(a, "Dramatic") - at(a, "None")
    }
    for (l in LEVELS) out[[paste(m, q, "AI minus Human", l, sep = "|")]] <- at("AI", l) - at("Human", l)
    out[[paste(m, q, "AI minus Human", "Dramatic minus None", sep = "|")]] <-
      (at("AI", "Dramatic") - at("AI", "None")) - (at("Human", "Dramatic") - at("Human", "None"))
  }
  do.call(cbind, out)
}

# The shares of one study from participant weights: each participant counts
# as many times as the weight says, one row of weights per resample.
shares_from <- function(sm, weights) {
  lapply(setNames(LABEL_LEVELS, LABEL_LEVELS), function(a) {
    ix <- which(sm$arm == a)
    w <- weights[[a]]
    lapply(setNames(names(MEASURE_NAMES), names(MEASURE_NAMES)), function(m) {
      (w %*% sm[[m]][ix, , drop = FALSE]) / (w %*% sm$n[ix, , drop = FALSE])
    })
  })
}

# The resamples are drawn study by study, Human arm first, from one seed.
set.seed(SEED)
observed <- list()
replicates <- list()
for (s in STUDY_LEVELS) {
  sm <- study_matrices[[s]]
  ones <- lapply(setNames(LABEL_LEVELS, LABEL_LEVELS),
                 function(a) matrix(1, 1, sum(sm$arm == a)))
  draws <- lapply(setNames(LABEL_LEVELS, LABEL_LEVELS), function(a) {
    n_arm <- sum(sm$arm == a)
    t(vapply(seq_len(N_BOOT), function(b) {
      tabulate(sample.int(n_arm, n_arm, replace = TRUE), nbins = n_arm)
    }, numeric(n_arm)))
  })
  observed[[s]] <- quantities(shares_from(sm, ones))
  replicates[[s]] <- quantities(shares_from(sm, draws))
}
observed[[SCOPES[1]]] <- Reduce(`+`, observed[STUDY_LEVELS]) / length(STUDY_LEVELS)
replicates[[SCOPES[1]]] <- Reduce(`+`, replicates[STUDY_LEVELS]) / length(STUDY_LEVELS)

# The number of explanations behind each share, by study and pooled.
n_by_study <- bind_rows(
  origin %>% count(study, arm = as.character(source), level, question = dimension),
  origin %>% count(study, arm = as.character(source), level) %>% mutate(question = QUESTIONS[1]))
n_explanations <- bind_rows(
  n_by_study %>% rename(scope = study),
  n_by_study %>% group_by(arm, level, question) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>% mutate(scope = SCOPES[1])) %>%
  rename(n_explanations = n)
origin_talk <- bind_rows(lapply(SCOPES, function(sc) {
  tibble(scope = sc, name = colnames(observed[[sc]]),
         estimate = as.numeric(observed[[sc]][1, ]),
         ci_lo = apply(replicates[[sc]], 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
         ci_hi = apply(replicates[[sc]], 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
         n_valid = colSums(!is.na(replicates[[sc]])))
})) %>%
  separate(name, into = c("mark", "question", "arm", "level"), sep = "\\|") %>%
  mutate(quantity = case_when(
    arm %in% LABEL_LEVELS & level %in% LEVELS ~ "share of explanations",
    arm %in% LABEL_LEVELS ~ "change in share, Dramatic minus None",
    level %in% LEVELS ~ "difference in share, AI minus Human",
    TRUE ~ "difference in the change, AI minus Human"),
    measure = MEASURE_NAMES[mark], B = N_BOOT, seed = SEED,
    resampled = "participants within study and arm, with replacement") %>%
  left_join(n_explanations, by = c("scope", "question", "arm", "level")) %>%
  select(scope, measure, question, quantity, arm, level, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi,
         n_explanations, n_valid, B, seed, resampled)
stopifnot(all(!is.na(origin_talk$n_explanations[origin_talk$quantity == "share of explanations"])))
write_table(origin_talk, "explanation_shift_origin_talk.csv")

print(as.data.frame(origin_talk %>%
  filter(question == QUESTIONS[1], scope == SCOPES[1]) %>%
  select(measure, quantity, arm, level, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi) %>%
  mutate(measure = sub(" \\(.*", "", measure), across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 4)))))

# The pooled result for each mark in words, over all three questions, in
# percentage points.
pick <- function(mk, arm, level) {
  origin_talk %>% filter(scope == SCOPES[1], question == QUESTIONS[1],
                         measure == MEASURE_NAMES[[mk]], arm == !!arm, level == !!level)
}
for (mk in names(MEASURE_NAMES)) {
  ai_none <- pick(mk, "AI", "None"); ai_dram <- pick(mk, "AI", "Dramatic")
  ai_ch <- pick(mk, "AI", "Dramatic minus None"); hu_ch <- pick(mk, "Human", "Dramatic minus None")
  did <- pick(mk, "AI minus Human", "Dramatic minus None")
  cat(sprintf(paste0("Explanations that %s, pooled: AI arm %.2f%% at None and %.2f%% at Dramatic, ",
                     "a change of %+.2f points (95%% interval %+.2f to %+.2f); Human arm change %+.2f ",
                     "points (%+.2f to %+.2f); AI minus Human in the change %+.2f points ",
                     "(%+.2f to %+.2f).\n"),
              c(prompt = "mention prompting or a machine",
                machine = "state that a machine made the work")[[mk]],
              100 * ai_none$estimate, 100 * ai_dram$estimate,
              100 * ai_ch$estimate, 100 * ai_ch$ci_lo, 100 * ai_ch$ci_hi,
              100 * hu_ch$estimate, 100 * hu_ch$ci_lo, 100 * hu_ch$ci_hi,
              100 * did$estimate, 100 * did$ci_lo, 100 * did$ci_hi))
}
```

# 5. The figure

The top row shows the estimated mean None to Dramatic shift of each arm on
creativity, within each study and pooled, with its 95 percent interval. A
lower point means the explanation at Dramatic stayed closer to the
participant's own explanation at None. The bottom rows show the share of
explanations, over all three questions, that mention prompting or a machine
and that state a machine made the work, at each level and in each arm, with
intervals from resampling participants. AI is drawn in black with solid lines
and Human in white with dashed lines. The caption states that the analysis is
exploratory.

```{r figure, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 9}
FIG_PDF <- file.path(FIGURES, "explanation_shift.pdf")
FIG_PNG <- file.path(FIGURES, "explanation_shift.png")
run_clear_outputs(run, FIG_PDF, FIG_PNG)

SCOPE_SHORT <- c("pooled over studies, equal weight" = "Pooled", "Study 2" = "Study 2",
                 "Study 4" = "Study 4", "Study 5" = "Study 5")
arm_scales <- list(
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Human = 21, AI = 21), name = "Source label"),
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Human = "white", AI = "black"), name = "Source label"))
arm_lines <- scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Human = "dashed", AI = "solid"), name = "Source label")
theme_fig <- theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = "grey60"))
dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.45)

panel_a <- arm_means %>%
  filter(dimension == "creativity") %>%
  mutate(scope = factor(SCOPE_SHORT[scope], levels = c("Study 2", "Study 4", "Study 5", "Pooled")),
         arm = factor(arm, levels = LABEL_LEVELS),
         distance = factor(paste(tools::toTitleCase(distance), "distance"),
                           levels = c("Embedding distance", "Word distance"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = scope, y = mean_shift, shape = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi), width = 0.15, position = dodge,
                colour = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, position = dodge, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ distance, scales = "free_y") +
  arm_scales +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean shift, None to Dramatic\n(distance minus stranger baseline)",
       title = "A. Creativity explanations: how far they moved from None to Dramatic") +
  theme_fig + theme(legend.position = "none")

panel_b <- origin_talk %>%
  filter(question == QUESTIONS[1], quantity == "share of explanations") %>%
  mutate(scope = factor(SCOPE_SHORT[scope], levels = c("Study 2", "Study 4", "Study 5", "Pooled")),
         arm = factor(arm, levels = LABEL_LEVELS),
         level = factor(level, levels = LEVELS),
         mark = factor(ifelse(grepl("^mentions", measure), "Mentions prompting\nor a machine",
                              "States a machine\nmade the work"),
                       levels = c("Mentions prompting\nor a machine", "States a machine\nmade the work"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = level, y = 100 * estimate, group = arm, shape = arm, fill = arm,
             linetype = arm)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = 100 * ci_lo, ymax = 100 * ci_hi), width = 0.12,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), linetype = "solid", colour = "black") +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), colour = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), colour = "black") +
  facet_grid(mark ~ scope, scales = "free_y") +
  arm_scales + arm_lines +
  labs(x = "Modification level", y = "Explanations, percent",
       title = "B. Talk of origin at each level, all three questions") +
  theme_fig

# The figure states the analysis status in its caption, as every table does
# in its first column.
fig <- (panel_a / panel_b) + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.5)) +
  plot_annotation(caption = paste(
    "Exploratory: specified on 9 October 2026, after the registered results of all five",
    "studies were known; no registration names it."),
    theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0)))
ggsave(FIG_PDF, fig, width = 9, height = 9, device = "pdf")
ggsave(FIG_PNG, fig, width = 9, height = 9, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
fig
```

# 6. Fit status

A fit converged when the optimizer reached a stable best fit and lme4, the
package that fits the models, raised no warning about it. A fit is singular
when a variance is estimated at zero, here the variance between source
images or between participants. A converged singular fit keeps its numbers,
under the rule of `shared/R/fit_status.R`; a fit that did not converge has
its intervals and p-values set to missing.

```{r fit-log}
# One row per observed mixed model, with its convergence status and the
# number of its 200 permutation refits that returned a fit and that converged.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TABLES, "explanation_shift_fit_log.csv"))
perm_counts <- models %>% filter(scope == SCOPES[1]) %>%
  transmute(step = paste0("3 shift, ", dimension, ", ", distance, " distance"),
            n_perm, n_perm_valid, n_perm_converged)
fit_log_tbl <- bind_rows(fit_log) %>%
  mutate(kind = "linear mixed model", usable = !fit_error & converged) %>%
  left_join(perm_counts, by = "step") %>%
  relocate(step, kind, usable)
write_table(fit_log_tbl, "explanation_shift_fit_log.csv")
print(as.data.frame(select(fit_log_tbl, step, n_obs, usable, converged, singular,
                           n_perm_valid, n_perm_converged)))
cat("Mixed models:", nrow(fit_log_tbl), "| converged:", sum(fit_log_tbl$converged),
    "| singular:", sum(fit_log_tbl$singular %in% TRUE),
    "| errored:", sum(fit_log_tbl$fit_error), "\n")
```
